transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-22
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Jules (Redwood SE), Erin (Redwood CSM), Maya (Blue Meridian SRE), Tom (Eng Lead), Priya (Product), Alan (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick weekly check-in for the POC focused on throughput optimization. Discussed last week's playback results, queueing jitter observed during a mid-day spike, tuned continuous-batching params, and talked through fallback policy when Dedicated capacity is exhausted. Agreed on playback test and artifact sharing.

Topics:
- Playback results review (10k request run)
- Batching windows and continuous batching aggressiveness
- Concurrency target adjustments and tail latency SLOs
- Queueing/backpressure and burst capacity fallback to hosted variants
- Next steps: playback run, logs, pricing, contract timing

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (AE): All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. we have about 40 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Maya (SRE): Hey, Maya here.
[00:10] Tom (Eng Lead): Tom here.
[00:12] Priya (Product): Priya.
[00:14] Alan (ML): Alan.
[00:16] Jules (SE): Jules on deck.
[00:18] Samir: Cool. Erin from CS?
[00:20] Erin (CSM): Hi all.
[00:22] Samir: Great. Quick recap — last week we ran the 10k playback and saw throughput plateau at about 8500 rps with spikes in tail latency when queue depth hit the soft threshold. Jules, want to walk through the logs?
[00:34] Jules: Yeah, sure. So I pulled the playback artifacts you sent, thank you Maya. The interesting bit — there were frequent short-lived queue bursts at t+12m and t+23m, those corresponded with larger prompt sizes from the product flow. Our continuous batching setup aggregated requests up to roughly 64 tokens beyond the normal distribution which delayed some critical low-latency requests. We saw KV cache hits drop during the burst windows which magnified cost.
[01:03] Maya: slight correction, the prompt size skew was actually from our new feedback flow, which sends longer context. We didn't think it'd change the batch distribution so much.
[01:10] Tom: right we rolled that out midday. we saw errors in our app logs that matched the timings.
[01:15] Jules: So two levers we tried: lower continuous-batch max-wait from 30ms to 12ms, and cap batch size at 48. That reduced tail P95 from about 420ms to 260ms under the same concurrency. But throughput dropped about 8% for steady-state because we reduced aggregation.
[01:36] Alan: is that because less batching means fewer consolidated kernels per step?
[01:39] Jules: exactly. More kernel invocations per token = slightly higher cost per token but better latency. It's the classic latency vs unit-cost tradeoff.
[01:45] Priya: Our tolerance for P95 is 300ms for the critical flow, anything higher impacts UX. So the 260ms is ok. But during spikes we saw P99 jump to 1.8s which is concern.
[01:57] Samir: Right, so we proposed a dynamic policy: keep aggressive batching at baseline for cost efficiency but when queue depth exceeds X (we used X=120) switch to concurrency bump and tighter batching window, and if Dedicated pool nears capacity, fallback to a lighter hosted model variant with pre-warmed instances.
[02:18] Maya: can you clarify what "fallback to hosted" means for data residency? All our traffic is PHI-adjacent and we need residency controls.
[02:26] Samir: Good point. For you we'd only use Hosted in the same region under a VPC-peered private path and with KMS keys you manage; logs are still obfuscated. But we should confirm that with security.
[02:38] Erin: We can share the private deployment runbook; for Blue Meridian we suggested a specific fallback policy that stays inside the VPC and uses dedicated model variants but on pooled infra — basically Dedicated-lite.
[02:48] Tom: okay, that sounds better. we need to confirm encryption/KMS details.
[02:52] Samir: We'll include the SOC2/ISO excerpt and the KMS integration doc in the follow-up.
[02:58] Jules: Back to tuning — we also experimented with concurrency cap. Under the original config concurrency=64, queueing backed up. We tested step-downs to 48 and 32. At 32 we saw more stable latency and the batching engine reached a sweet spot: still consolidated enough requests but not holding for long tail prompts. That gave us ~8200 rps steady with P95 under 300ms and much better P99 percentiles.
[03:31] Maya: is 32 a hard cap or just a target? Because our upstream autoscaler also adjusts replicas and sometimes spikes concurrency per instance.
[03:38] Jules: it's a per-instance concurrency target; autoscaler controls instance count. Ideally, set target concurrency=32 and let the autoscaler add nodes to absorb sustained increases. For short bursts we use burst-capacity (reserve pool) to avoid cold starts.
[03:50] Alan: about reserve pool — in the playback with spikes we hit the soft limit and we saw fallback attempts that didn't fully spin up in time. Is that a cold-start problem or a routing issue?
[03:58] Jules: Mostly cold-start; the fallback model variant wasn't pre-warmed enough. We recommend a small buffer of pre-warmed slots and a fast-spin path for critical flows. That costs a little, but saves user-visible errors.
[04:09] Tom: what's the expected cost impact of pre-warming say 3 instances in our region?
[04:12] Samir: I'll send the math in the pricing sheet, but ballpark it's a few hundred dollars/day depending on instance type and whether quantized model is used. We'll show a delta.
[04:22] Priya: Can Redwood do adaptive pre-warm — like spin up based on predicted daily cadence?
[04:26] Jules: Yep, we have adaptive tooling. For this POC we can keep a fixed pre-warm and then toggle adaptive predictions once we have 7 days of traces.
[04:35] Maya: we can provide 48 hours today. After that we'll need a longer sample.
[04:39] Samir: Perfect. Maya, please share S3 link with logs.
[04:43] Maya: will do.
[04:45] Samir: Also, regarding continuous batching parameters — we recommended three small changes: max-wait 12ms, max-batch 48, and enable prompt-size-aware batching which deprioritizes long-context requests when latency SLO is close to breach. That last one is opt-in; do you want us to enable it?
[05:05] Priya: yes, opt-in seems fine for the critical flow. For non-critical flows keep default to maximize efficiency.
[05:11] Tom: any risk of lost requests if we deprioritize?
[05:13] Jules: not lost — just queued slightly longer or routed to fallback model which has larger context window. We'll add a route that keeps long-context requests on a different lane.
[05:21] Alan: can we see the config snippets?
[05:23] Jules: I'll paste them in the follow-up. They are small yaml blocks — concurrency_target: 32, continuous_batching: { max_wait_ms: 12, max_batch_tokens: 48, prompt_size_aware: true }, fallback_policy: { threshold_queue: 120, fallback_variant: hosted-lite, prewarm_slots: 3 }
[05:46] Maya: quick note: the transcript earlier said KV cash instead of KV cache, fyi.
[05:51] Samir: thanks. we have some transcription hiccups.
[05:54] Priya: anything about cost per 1M tokens after these changes?
[05:58] Samir: We'll include cost delta in the pricing sheet — it's mostly driven by the percent of time we run in lower-batching mode and any pre-warms. We gave a sample scenario in the deck: worst-case +14% unit cost, typical -6% with caching and batching.
[06:15] Tom: Regarding metrics — can we get token-level billing mapped to route? We want per-endpoint cost to see which flows drive cost.
[06:21] Erin: Redwood Console exports per-route token breakdown; we'll set up a dashboard and give you RBAC access for product and finance.
[06:29] Maya: security question: what about audit logs for fallback events? We need to record when traffic routed off Dedicated.
[06:35] Samir: Audit logs are available with timestamps and reason codes. We'll show sample logs in the follow-up.
[06:41] Jules: Also ran a simulation of progressive batching: when queue depth grows stepwise, we incrementally reduce batch window then bump concurrency. That avoided a large P99 spike in sims. We'll run the real 10k playback with progressive policy as next artifact.
[06:55] Priya: timeline?
[06:57] Jules: I can run it tomorrow and send artifacts by Monday EOD.
[07:01] Maya: we need it by Tuesday so we can align with our sprint planning.
[07:04] Samir: We'll aim for Monday EOD.
[07:06] Tom: any blockers from Redwood infra side?
[07:08] Jules: nothing immediate. We may need the 48h traces to tune the prediction model for adaptive pre-warm.
[07:15] Samir: Recap next steps: Jules runs 10k playback with concurrency target 32 + progressive batching and shares logs; Maya uploads 48h trace; Samir sends pricing & SOC2/KMS excerpt; Priya confirms PO timing.
[07:28] Priya: I'll follow up with procurement questions by Friday.
[07:31] Maya: sending trace within the hour.
[07:33] Samir: Great. Any final questions?
[07:36] Alan: one small ask — can we get a short doc on how fallback variants affect semantic fidelity? We saw some minor changes in completions when switching models.
[07:45] Jules: yes, we'll include a short note about model deltas and suggested eval prompts to check fidelity.
[07:51] Samir: awesome. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with artifacts.
[07:55] Tom: Thanks.
[07:56] Meeting ends.
